clue.text: Approximate price semi may make

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be made into something new, so they are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rough figure for what a semi-detached house might fetch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approximate' looks like a verb but is the adjective definition; 'may make' tells you to rearrange PRICE SEMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something approximate is not exact, which is a synonym sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Victor out West is a pretty good shot

indicators.note: signals that a letter is put out of the word for victor

parts.note: a victor is the winner of a contest

explanation.surface: A gunfighter from out West proves a decent marksman.
explanation.walkthrough: In archery and rifle shooting the inner is the ring just outside the bull, so a hit there is good but not perfect. 'out' removes the W.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target the ring next to the bullseye scores well, a near-miss example of good shooting.

clue.text: Picnic arranged to entertain posh composer

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the shuffled letters hold a guest letter
the letters of the word picnic are set out in a fresh order

parts.note: U is the crossword convention for upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A smart picnic party is laid on for a visiting composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles PICNIC to PCCINI-style letters, and 'to entertain' puts U inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini was the Italian opera composer of La Bohème and Tosca, an example of the category.

clue.text: Pick hat up and finally leave

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a hat, puts it on and then walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TILE into ELIT; 'finally' adds the E ending 'leave'. TILE as slang for a hat is dated British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group is its best members, the same sense as the select few.

clue.text: It's not right for in-law to embrace divorcee

parts.note: taken as written
an ex is a former spouse, a divorcee
an act is a law passed by parliament

explanation.surface: A remark that it is wrong for a son-in-law to hug a divorced woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in-law' looks like a relative by marriage, but splits into two words; 'to embrace' signals the divorcee goes inside the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise or not correct, a synonym of not right.

clue.text: Like jelly in pineapple?

parts.note: jelly is slang for gelignite and pineapple is slang for a hand grenade, so the filling of one is blasting stuff

explanation.surface: A dessert question about fruit set in jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite inside a grenade is a blasting agent, so the description fits a detonating substance.

clue.text: People available for a game

definitions.meaning: a group of people on call
a cue game like billiards played on a table with pockets

explanation.definitionFit: A pool is both a reserve of workers to draw on and a pocket billiards game.

clue.text: Fond of, to some extent

explanation.definitionFit: Partial means having a liking for, and also incomplete or only part done.

clue.text: Not on time when trade is slack

parts.note: a light that is not on is off
a season is a time of year

explanation.surface: A trader complains of not being punctual during a quiet period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on time' reads as late, but must be split after 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiet part of the year in tourism or retail, when business is slow.

clue.text: Write letters in bed, when in quarters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: says the bed sits inside the quarters

parts.note: S and E are two compass quarters, south and east
a crib is a baby's bed

explanation.surface: Writing letters while lying in bed in one's lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings, but gives compass points S and E around CRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to write or carve lettering, for example on a stone or in a book.

clue.text: Make clear there's a fantastic fry-up about one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round another
something fantastic is wild and strange, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone clears the air by cooking a splendid fried breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges FRYUP, and 'about' puts it round I. A fry-up is a British cooked breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: To purify is to remove impurities, making water or air clean and clear.

clue.text: Note more money for cook

parts.note: B is a musical note
a raise is a pay rise, more money

explanation.surface: A cook writes a memo asking for a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a memo but is the letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is a cooking method, slow-cooking meat in a little liquid in a lidded pot.

clue.text: Suffered, so gained redress

indicators.note: to redress is to put right again, so the letters are reset

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who suffered wrongs eventually won compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redress' looks like compensation, but signals a reordering of SO GAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised means having endured great distress or pain, a synonym of suffered.

clue.text: In Latin "I" is used by many showing vanity

parts.note: ego is the Latin word for I
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, read as many

explanation.surface: A grammar note that the Latin first person is beloved of the conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: M as 'many' comes from the Roman numeral for 1000.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is self-centredness and conceit, close in sense to vanity.

clue.text: Where stevedores work for a likable chap

definitions.meaning: dock workers load freight at a harbour for cargo
someone who takes a joke or a loss cheerfully

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a cargo harbour; as an idiom it is a pleasant, uncomplaining person.

clue.text: Promises of party in show ring

parts.note: to manifest is to show plainly
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A party sets out its promises at a show in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A political party's published list of policies and pledges before an election.

clue.text: Court case: it's arranged so this person may prove their promise

definitions.text: this person may prove their promise

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court

indicators.note: the letters of the word are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Legal arrangements are made for a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reorders ITS into IST. A trialist is a sports player given a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A trialist is a player on trial for a team, who gets the chance to show their ability.

clue.text: Swindle made to pay — but jailed all the same

parts.note: a con is a swindle
someone fined has been made to pay a penalty

explanation.surface: A fraudster was fined but still ended up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all the same' is a link, meaning nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confined means being shut in or locked up, as a prisoner is.

clue.text: Leading at snooker — a conspiracy?

definitions.meaning: ahead by a game, a frame being one game of snooker
a plot to make an innocent person look guilty

explanation.definitionFit: Frame up reads as ahead by a frame in snooker, and as a noun means a plot to incriminate someone.

clue.text: Big drinks bring people to court

definitions.meaning: a double is twice the usual measure of spirits
the tennis match for pairs puts four players on court

explanation.definitionFit: Doubles are double measures of spirits, and the tennis format for two pairs.

clue.text: Get in a pie — for this?

definitions.text: Get in a pie — for this?

indicators.note: printer's pie is type jumbled together, so it signals a mix-up of letters

explanation.surface: A question about why you would get into a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' looks like food, but is the printing term for scrambled type, rearranging GET IN A; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting stuck into a pie is consuming it, which is what the clue asks the purpose of.

clue.text: Upsetting habit in restaurants?

definitions.meaning: the custom of leaving extra money for the waiter

explanation.definitionFit: Tipping means overturning something, and also giving gratuities to staff.

clue.text: Gold in finals round? Quite the opposite, resulting in a serious complaint

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
says the containment is reversed, so the other piece goes inside the gold

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: round suggests turning about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gold medal in the last round of a competition, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, gold goes inside the anagram of FINALS ('round'); 'Quite the opposite' flips it so the scrambled letters go inside gold's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Asian flu was a serious influenza pandemic of 1957, an example of a grave illness.

clue.text: Put down for PE, does workout

indicators.note: a workout puts things through their paces, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school PE lesson involves someone doing exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' looks like writing down, but means to oust from power.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to remove them from office, to put them down.

clue.text: A mouthful of water

parts.note: the mouth of a river, where it splits into many channels, is full of water

explanation.surface: Someone takes a sip of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A river mouth spreading into channels over silt is this landform, as with the Nile.

clue.text: Full-bodied drink

definitions.meaning: a dark beer such as porter

explanation.definitionFit: Stout means portly or plump, and is also a strong dark beer.

clue.text: Do they keep to the beaten track?

definitions.text: Do they keep to the beaten track?

parts.words: Do they keep to the beaten track?
parts.note: beaten reads as defeated, so those who are beaten on the race track are the ones who lose

explanation.surface: A question about walkers who stick to well-trodden paths.
explanation.definitionFit: Those defeated in a race are the beaten ones, the non-winners.

clue.text: Sweet sort of lady giving children guidance

definitions.text: sort of lady giving children guidance
definitions.meaning: a British school crossing warden carries a round sign on a pole and is known by this name

explanation.definitionFit: It is a sugary treat on a stick, and the nickname for a British road crossing patrol warden.

clue.text: Kitty's back to stay

indicators.note: back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a kitty is a pot of shared money, so the kitty's is the pot's

explanation.surface: The cat returns to stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a cat but is the money pot; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to halt or remain, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Talons hug brutally in attack

indicators.note: brutally suggests violent rough handling, so the letters are mangled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird of prey grips its victim savagely with its claws.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce assault, a synonym for an attack.
